problems.problem: `--web` is accepted but silently ignored for all three commands. I verified with commander (v11, same config as this repo) that `capy transport --web` parses and reaches the action; the action never reads `optsWithGlobals().web`, so the TERMINAL path runs and the redeem code — a bearer credential for the whole account — is still printed to stdout. That is precisely the leak this parcel exists to close, and `capy recover --web` likewise falls through to a dead TTY prompt (the exact bug index.ts:663-667 documents for `capy add --web`). The parcel rules forbid touching index.ts and the report discloses this, so it is not the agent's defect — but the flag is live-and-ignored today, which is worse than absent, and the coordinator must wire lines 550/642/651.

`--web` changes what gets DELETED, not only how a question is rendered. With plaintext present and NO recovery session open, the terminal path returns early ('No recovery session active.') and removes nothing; `executeInBrowser` (line 132) offers the sweep anyway, and I confirmed by clicking that every row arrives PRE-TICKED, so the default submit unlinks files the terminal would never have touched. Disclosed in the report and defensible as a product decision, but it violates the brief's '--web changes the RENDERING of a question, never the logic ... or what gets written' and deserves an explicit owner sign-off rather than landing inside a rendering parcel.

The `unverified` fork — the one genuinely NEW control this parcel invents (a danger submit that writes a master key under a guessed KDF version when the trial decryption could not run) — has no browser test. It is exercised only by fetch against the loopback (tests/ui/recoveryScreens.test.ts:359-458), which is exactly the gap the brief says killed three inventions this session. I wrote and ran a throwaway CDP test against the real page: `answer:()=>({writeUnverified:!0})` exists in the compiled screen, the danger submit is gated on a consent box, and clicking it writes once with `kdfVersion` null — so it does work, but the branch shipped unclicked. Same for the no-session end-recover sweep and the transport `Cancel` button (both of which I also clicked and both of which pass).

`capy transport` reaches `resolveOrgContext`, which itself asks an inquirer `list` ('Select organization:', src/core/orgContext.ts:50) when there is no keep.lock and more than one org. That prompt has no `--web` path, so once index.ts is wired, `capy transport --web` can still block on a TTY question before the browser ever opens. The file is shared (invite/kick/users) and outside the parcel, so leaving it is correct — but it is an unclosed hole in 'every prompt in this flow has a --web path' and belongs on the coordinator's list.

The `manual: true` branch (line 84) is unreachable from the product: `buildRecoverData` hardcodes `signedIn: true` (src/ui/recoveryScreens.ts:211) because `recover` authenticates before it serves anything, so the only dotted-track stop the rail can draw is never drawn. It is exercised solely by tests/core/recoverPlan.test.ts. Harmless, and arguably correct for a future `--json`, but the contract's `manual` modifier currently has no live producer here.

`readSessionSummary()` puts the organization's UUID into `session.orgName`, so the page reads 'Session for  b3f1…'. Disclosed, and fixing it means writing the name at `saveRecoverySession` time in src/config/globalConfig.ts (out of parcel), but the payload field is named `orgName` and does not carry one.

The new browser tests select by `[role=radio]`/`[role=checkbox]` + `.label` text and by button copy ('Use this organization', 'Overwrite key', 'Recover key', 'End session and delete', 'Close this out') because these three screens carry no `data-test` hooks the way `sync-conflict` does. Any copy edit in packages/ui breaks them with a `.find(...)` TypeError rather than a readable failure. Worth a `data-test` request to the packages/ui owner.
